interface.title: River Outlook (with a 'How This Works' documentation page)
interface.field: Hydrology / water-resources engineering (stochastic streamflow generation, flood frequency)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis and design: turning a short measured record into long synthetic records, design flows and validation checks
interface.what_it_is_for: Generating long synthetic monthly discharge records for the Hadejia River in Nigeria from a precomputed seasonally standardised ARIMA(1,0,0) model, then reading off return-period design flows and comparing the synthetic record with the 26-year measured record.

data.note: The app reads a precomputed results file (model coefficients, 12 monthly seasonal means and SDs, validation and method-comparison results) for the Hadejia River at Hadejia (GRDC 1837401, Jan 1980 – Feb 2006, 26 years). The Conecuh River (Alabama) appears only as text and numbers in the 'For the curious' panel and on the documentation page. There is no uploader and no river selector. No seed is set, so values change on every press of Generate.

features.name: Length + ensemble-size generator panel with presets
features.general: Pick a simulation length from preset buttons or a bounded number field, set how many independent realisations to pool, see a live summary of the total sample size, then run
features.specific: 30/100/500/1,000 yr presets plus 'Number of years to generate' (1–10,000) and 'Independent records' steppers, a live line ('100 years = 1,200 monthly values per record, 2,000 synthetic years in total'), and the 'Generate synthetic record' button
steps: click a preset or type a number of years
optionally set the number of independent records with the field or the +/− steppers
read the live total-sample summary line
press Generate synthetic record
an out-of-range entry greys the + stepper and shows 'Press Enter to apply'; once committed (e.g. Tab away) the field turns red with a range tooltip (1–10,000)
serves_tasks: Choose the length of the synthetic series
Choose how many independent realisations to pool
Run the generator and inspect the synthetic series

features.name: Generated time-series table with search, sort and CSV export
features.general: Show a long generated series as a scrollable grid you can search and sort, and export it as CSV
features.specific: Year / Month / Discharge (m³/s) data grid for the first record, with toolbar (show/hide columns, search, fullscreen), header sort, and a 'Download this record as CSV (N rows)' button
steps: generate a record
click the Search icon and type a term (e.g. 'Sep')
click a column header to sort
press 'Download this record as CSV'
serves_tasks: Run the generator and inspect the synthetic series

features.name: Return-period design-flow table and chart
features.general: Rank the yearly maxima pooled across realisations, report event magnitudes for standard return periods as a table and a log-x curve with a reference line at the largest observed value, and drop return periods the sample is too short to support
features.specific: 'What a design calculation reads off it': table of Return period / Chance/yr / Design flow and a Vega line chart on a log return-period axis with a dashed line at the measured maximum (139 m³/s); tooltips on points; Show data / PNG / Vega-Lite spec toolbar
steps: generate a record
scroll the table sideways to read the design flows
hover chart points for exact values
regenerate or lengthen the record to see how the tail estimates move
export via Show data, Download as PNG or Copy Vega-Lite spec
serves_tasks: Read event magnitudes for standard return periods

features.name: Synthetic-vs-observed comparison panel
features.general: Set a simulated sample beside the observed sample: two side-by-side stat cards, an overlaid histogram, and an overlaid exceedance (duration) curve on a log scale
features.specific: 'Generated record — extremes' card (with the 5/7 Reasonable tag) next to 'The measured record' card, plus a histogram of monthly values (upper 0.5% trimmed) and a flow-duration curve, each with a fullscreen option

compare the mean, SD and extremes in the two cards (percentiles are shown for the generated record only)
open the flow-duration curve full-screen to see where the lines separate
open the histogram full-screen and hover bars for counts

click the expander below the results
read the coefficients, standard errors and AIC
read the 12-month seasonal parameter table

features.name: Held-out property-validation table

screens_never_reached: Any Conecuh River output: it appears only as text and numbers; there is no control to generate or view Conecuh records
A displayed ARCH or Jarque–Bera result: the documentation names both tests, but no value is shown anywhere in the interface
A 'band' or ensemble-median line: the documentation mentions one, but no such chart appears on River Outlook
not_done: Checking the ARCH residual diagnostic (README goal): the interface shows only the Ljung–Box p (0.127 / 0.1266). ARCH is named in the documentation without a value.

Downloading the return-period table from its data-grid toolbar: clicking its download icon produced no file (screens/026.webp). The main 'Download this record as CSV' button and chart PNG export did work.

Bug: generating 1 year × 1 record crashes the page with KeyError: 'Return period' (pages/0_Forecast.py line 363). The return-period section shows 'empty' and the right-hand extremes panel disappears (screens/049.webp, screens/050.webp). With 15 synthetic years only the 2/5/10-yr periods appear (screens/051.webp).

Quirk: typing 50000 into years is rejected ('Number is outside the allowed range… between 1 and 10000', red field; screens/027.webp, screens/028.webp). While the field holds that invalid value, clicking the 500 yr preset does not replace it, and Generate silently runs the last valid value (1,000 yr × 6) (screens/029.webp, screens/030.webp).

Quirk: after switching to How This Works and back, the previous result (500 yr) is still shown, but the inputs have reset to 100 / 20, so the form no longer matches the displayed record (screens/039.webp).

The documentation contradicts the main page: it says ADF rejects a unit root and KPSS does not reject stationarity at d = 0 (screens/034.webp), while the expander says ADF −0.980 does not reject and KPSS 1.448 rejects, so the tests indicate d = 1 (screens/015.webp). Its differencing example (~10^10 m³/s vs 16.4, the Conecuh mean) also differs from the expander's Hadejia figures (1.57e+24 vs 24.3). The expander's method-comparison table also gives Ljung–Box p 0.059 for standardisation, not the 0.127 on the summary card (check/screens/024.webp).

Usability: the histogram uses raw counts, so the 314 measured months are nearly invisible next to tens of thousands of synthetic months (screens/045.webp). The legends are not interactive, and the flow-duration curve has no hover tooltip.

Tail estimates move a lot between runs (500-yr flow 436, 562 and 817 m³/s across three runs: screens/010.webp, screens/040.webp, screens/022.webp). The app shows no confidence interval for them, which matches the 'parameters treated as known' limitation in the documentation.
Not explored: the Streamlit 'Main menu' and 'Deploy' (app framework controls, not scientific features), and the 'How this works →' link (it goes to the same Documentation page as the top navigation).
